ping.title: Check the connection
ping.description: Ping AvaTax and read back whether the credentials authenticated. The cheapest call there is, and the one that tells you whether a 401 is the account id, the licence key, or the wrong host.

output.description: The ping result, including `authenticated`, the account and the AvaTax version.

list_subscriptions.title: List the account's subscriptions
list_subscriptions.description: Read which AvaTax services the account is subscribed to. Worth checking before an endpoint 403s: certificates, returns and cross-border each need their own subscription.

create_transaction.title: Calculate tax (and optionally record a document)
create_transaction.description: Calculate tax for a transaction. `type` decides whether anything is recorded: "SalesOrder" is a quote and stores nothing, "SalesInvoice" creates a document Avalara can file from. `commit: true` makes that document reportable immediately. `lines` carries the items, each with an amount and optionally a tax code; `addresses` carries ship-from and ship-to, which is what actually decides the rate.

type.description: What kind of transaction this is. "SalesOrder" only quotes; "SalesInvoice" records a document. The Purchase and Return variants are the inbound and credit equivalents.

company_code.description: The company the transaction belongs to, by its company code.

date.description: Transaction date as YYYY-MM-DD -- this decides which tax rates apply.

customer_code.description: Your own code for the customer. Exemption certificates are matched on this, so it must be the same code you filed them under.

lines.description: The line items, each {"number": "1", "amount": 100.0, optionally "quantity", "itemCode", "taxCode", "description" and per-line "addresses"}.

addresses.description: Where the sale happens, e.g. {"shipFrom": {...}, "shipTo": {...}} with line1, city, region, postalCode and country. Alternatively use "singleLocation". This is what determines jurisdiction.

code.description: Your own document code. Reusing one is how a document is replaced -- leave it out and Avalara generates one.

commit.description: Commit the document immediately, making it reportable. Only meaningful for invoice types.

exemption_no.description: An exemption certificate number to apply to the whole transaction.

entity_use_code.description: Why the customer is exempt, as an entity-use code from list_entity_use_codes -- e.g. "A" for a federal government body.

reference_code.description: Your own reference for the transaction.

discount.description: A discount applied across the transaction.

salesperson_code.description: Your own code for the salesperson.

business_identification_no.description: The customer's VAT or business registration number, for cross-border.

include.description: Extra detail to return, e.g. "Lines,Details,Summary" or "Addresses".

output.description: The calculated transaction -- totals, per-line tax, and the jurisdiction detail behind each amount.

create_or_adjust_transaction.title: Create or correct a transaction in one call
create_or_adjust_transaction.description: Create a document, or -- if one already exists with the same code -- adjust it to match what you send. The idempotent way to keep AvaTax in step with an order that changed, without deciding up front whether it is new.

transaction.description: The transaction, in the same shape create_transaction's body takes -- `type`, `companyCode`, `date`, `customerCode`, `code`, `lines`, `addresses`.

list_transactions.title: List a company's transactions
list_transactions.description: Read the documents recorded for a company, newest first. `filter` takes Avalara's filter syntax -- e.g. "status eq Committed" or "date gt 2026-01-01" -- which is how you find what still needs committing.

filter.description: Avalara filter expression, e.g. "status eq Committed and totalTax gt 0".

skip.description: How many to skip, for paging.

data_source_id.description: Only transactions from this data source.

get_transaction.title: Get a transaction
get_transaction.description: Read one recorded document by its code -- status, totals and, with `include`, its lines and jurisdiction detail. `document_type` is needed when the same code exists as more than one type.

document_type.description: Which document type to read, when the code is ambiguous.

commit_transaction.title: Commit a transaction
commit_transaction.description: Mark a document as committed, which makes it reportable and includes it in the returns Avalara files. In production this is the moment a transaction becomes a compliance record -- uncommitting is possible but leaves a trail.

commit.description: True to commit. Sending false uncommits the document.

document_type.description: Which document type to act on.

uncommit_transaction.title: Uncommit a transaction
uncommit_transaction.description: Take a committed document back out of reporting so it can be corrected. Only possible while the period is still open -- once Avalara has filed the return, an adjustment is the only route.

document_type.description: Which document type to act on.

void_transaction.title: Void a transaction
void_transaction.description: Cancel a document. `code` says why -- "DocVoided" for a cancelled sale, "PostFailed" when your own system failed to post it. The document remains for audit but stops being reportable. Not reversible except through unvoid_transaction.

void_reason.description: Why the document is being voided.

unvoid_transaction.title: Unvoid a transaction
unvoid_transaction.description: Restore a voided document to its previous state -- the undo for a void applied in error.

document_type.description: Which document type to act on.

adjust_transaction.title: Adjust a transaction
adjust_transaction.description: Correct a recorded document by writing a new version of it. The original is kept and superseded, which is what an audit expects -- `adjustment_reason` and `adjustment_description` say why.

adjustment_reason.description: Why the document is being corrected.

new_transaction.description: The corrected transaction in full, in the same shape create_transaction's body takes. It replaces the original.

adjustment_description.description: Free-text explanation kept with the adjustment.

refund_transaction.title: Refund a transaction
refund_transaction.description: Create a refund document from an existing invoice -- full, partial, by percentage or for specific lines. Avalara writes the inverse document rather than editing the original, so both appear in the returns.

refund_date.description: Date of the refund as YYYY-MM-DD; decides which period it lands in.

refund_type.description: What is being refunded -- the whole document, a percentage, specific lines, or tax only.

refund_lines.description: Line numbers to refund, when `refund_type` is "Partial".

refund_transaction_code.description: Your own code for the refund document. Generated when omitted.

reference_code.description: Your own reference for the refund.

document_type.description: Which document type is being refunded.

use_tax_date_override.description: Use the refund date as the tax date rather than the original's.

settle_transaction.title: Settle a transaction
settle_transaction.description: Apply several changes to a document in one call -- verify its totals, change its code, and commit it. Convenient, and correspondingly easy to commit something you meant only to check.

verify.description: Expected totals to check against, e.g. {"verifyTransactionAmount": 100.0}.

document_type.description: Which document type to act on.

verify_transaction.title: Verify a transaction's totals
verify_transaction.description: Check that AvaTax's recorded amount and tax match what your own system believes -- the reconciliation call, which fails loudly rather than silently diverging.

verify_transaction_date.description: The date you expect on the document, YYYY-MM-DD.

change_transaction_code.title: Change a transaction's code
change_transaction_code.description: Rename a document. Useful when your own system's invoice number changed after the fact and the codes must line up for reconciliation.

document_type.description: Which document type to act on.

output.description: The transaction with its new code.

lock_transaction.title: Lock a transaction
lock_transaction.description: Lock a document so it cannot be changed. Avalara locks documents itself when a return is filed; doing it by hand needs the account to be configured for it.

is_locked.description: True to lock the document, false to unlock it.

document_type.description: Which document type to act on.

output.description: The transaction after the lock change.

audit_transaction.title: Audit a transaction
audit_transaction.description: Read the original API request that created a document, exactly as it was sent. The answer to "why did AvaTax calculate that" -- it shows the addresses and codes it actually received.

output.description: The original request and the reconstruction of the calculation.

create_multi_document_transaction.title: Create a multi-company transaction
create_multi_document_transaction.description: Record one economic event that spans several companies -- a drop-ship, an inter-company transfer -- as a set of linked documents Avalara keeps consistent.

transaction.description: The multi-document transaction -- `code`, `type`, `companyCode`, `date`, `customerCode` and `lines`, where each line names the company it belongs to.

resolve_address.title: Validate and resolve an address
resolve_address.description: Normalise an address and return the jurisdictions it falls in, with latitude and longitude. Run this before recording transactions in bulk: an unresolvable address is the usual reason tax comes out wrong.

region.description: State, province or region code, e.g. "CA".

output.description: The resolved address, its coordinates, the taxing jurisdictions and any validation messages.

get_tax_rates_by_address.title: Get tax rates for an address
get_tax_rates_by_address.description: Look up the combined rate at an address. This is a **rate lookup, not a calculation** -- it ignores nexus, product taxability and exemptions, and Avalara says not to use it to compute what to charge. Use create_transaction for that.

output.description: The total rate and the per-jurisdiction rates behind it.

get_tax_rates_by_postal_code.title: Get tax rates for a postal code
get_tax_rates_by_postal_code.description: Look up the combined rate for a country and postal code. Same caveat as get_tax_rates_by_address -- an estimate, not a calculation, and a postal code can straddle jurisdictions.

output.description: The total rate and its jurisdiction breakdown.

list_jurisdictions_by_address.title: List jurisdictions near an address
list_jurisdictions_by_address.description: Read the taxing jurisdictions covering an address -- state, county, city, special districts -- which is what a rate is actually the sum of.

list_companies.title: List companies
list_companies.description: Read the companies on the account, with their codes and ids. Almost everything else is scoped to one of them, so this is usually the first call -- note that transactions are addressed by company **code** and most configuration by company **id**.

filter.description: Avalara filter expression, e.g. "isActive eq true".

get_company.title: Get a company
get_company.description: Read one company by id -- its code, name, address and configuration flags.

initialize_company.title: Create a company with its default setup
initialize_company.description: Create a company and have Avalara build its default location, nexus and settings from the address given. The recommended way to onboard a company -- create_companies makes a bare record you then have to configure.

company_code.description: Your own code for the company; transactions reference it.

line1.description: Street address of the company's primary location.

taxpayer_id_number.description: The company's tax registration number, e.g. its EIN.

vat_registration_id.description: VAT registration number, for non-US companies.

output.description: The created company with the nexus, location and settings Avalara built.

create_companies.title: Create companies
create_companies.description: Create one or more bare company records. They have no nexus or locations until you add them, so nothing calculates tax yet -- initialize_company is usually the better call.

companies.description: The companies to create, each with at least `companyCode`, `name` and an address.

update_company.title: Update a company
update_company.description: Replace a company's record. This is a full update -- read it first with get_company and send back everything you want kept.

company.description: The complete company record, as get_company returns it.

list_company_nexus.title: List a company's nexus
list_company_nexus.description: Read the jurisdictions a company has declared nexus in. Nexus is what makes AvaTax charge tax at all -- a state with no nexus returns zero tax rather than an error, which is the single most common "why is tax missing" cause.

filter.description: Avalara filter expression, e.g. "country eq US".

top.description: How many nexus records to return.

create_nexus.title: Declare nexus
create_nexus.description: Declare that a company has nexus in one or more jurisdictions. Each entry must be copied from the definitions list (list_nexus_definitions) -- you cannot invent one -- and declaring nexus makes the company liable to collect there, so it is a compliance decision, not a settings change.

nexus.description: The nexus declarations, each an object copied from list_nexus_definitions with your `effectiveDate` and `nexusTypeId` filled in.

declare_nexus_by_address.title: Declare nexus by address
declare_nexus_by_address.description: Have Avalara work out which jurisdictions an address implies and declare nexus for them. The easier route than assembling definition objects by hand -- and it still creates real liability.

addresses.description: Addresses whose jurisdictions should get nexus, each with line1, city, region, postalCode and country.

output.description: The nexus records created for those addresses.

delete_nexus.title: Delete a nexus declaration
delete_nexus.description: Remove a nexus declaration. The company stops collecting tax there for new transactions -- past documents are untouched. Getting this wrong means under-collecting, so check the effective dates first.

output.description: Confirmation that the nexus was removed.

list_nexus_definitions.title: List all nexus definitions
list_nexus_definitions.description: Read every jurisdiction Avalara supports nexus in, with the exact objects create_nexus expects. This is the catalogue you copy from.

filter.description: Avalara filter expression, e.g. "country eq US and region eq CA".

list_nexus_by_address.title: List nexus definitions for an address
list_nexus_by_address.description: Read which nexus definitions apply to a given address -- the narrow version of list_nexus_definitions, and what declare_nexus_by_address uses internally.

output.description: The nexus definitions covering that address.

list_locations.title: List a company's locations
list_locations.description: Read a company's registered locations -- stores, warehouses, offices. Locations feed both nexus and origin-based sourcing, so a missing one changes the tax.

create_locations.title: Create locations
create_locations.description: Add locations to a company. `addressTypeId` and `addressCategoryId` decide how the location is treated for sourcing, and validate_location will tell you whether Avalara accepts the address.

locations.description: The locations to create, each with `locationCode`, `addressTypeId`, `addressCategoryId`, `line1`, `city`, `region`, `postalCode` and `country`.

validate_location.title: Validate a location
validate_location.description: Check whether a saved location's address is complete and resolvable. Worth running after a bulk import, since an invalid location silently distorts sourcing.

output.description: The validation result and any problems found.

delete_location.title: Delete a location
delete_location.description: Remove a location from a company. Sourcing for new transactions changes accordingly; recorded documents are untouched.

output.description: Confirmation that the location was deleted.

list_items.title: List a company's items
list_items.description: Read the company's item catalogue with the tax code mapped to each. An item's tax code is what decides whether it is taxable, exempt or reduced rate in each jurisdiction.

filter.description: Avalara filter expression, e.g. "taxCode eq P0000000".

get_item.title: Get an item
get_item.description: Read one catalogue item -- its code, tax code, description and classifications.

create_items.title: Create items
create_items.description: Add items to the company's catalogue, each mapping your own item code to an Avalara tax code. Once an item exists, a transaction line can name `itemCode` instead of repeating `taxCode`.

items.description: The items to create, each with `itemCode`, `description` and `taxCode` (from list_tax_codes).

update_item.title: Update an item
update_item.description: Replace an item's record -- most often to change its tax code, which changes how future transactions treat it.

item.description: The complete item record, as get_item returns it.

delete_item.title: Delete an item
delete_item.description: Remove an item from the catalogue. Transaction lines naming its item code fall back to whatever tax code they carry themselves.

output.description: Confirmation that the item was deleted.

sync_items.title: Sync items in bulk
sync_items.description: Upsert a batch of items in one call -- the maintenance path for a catalogue that lives in your own system and is mirrored here.

items.description: The items to create or update, each with `itemCode` and `taxCode`.

output.description: What the sync created and updated.

get_item_tax_code_recommendations.title: Get tax code recommendations for an item
get_item_tax_code_recommendations.description: Ask Avalara which tax code an item's description suggests -- the classification help for a catalogue where nobody knows whether a product is a "digital good" or "software as a service".

output.description: Recommended tax codes with confidence scores.

list_tax_codes.title: List Avalara tax codes
list_tax_codes.description: Read Avalara's tax code catalogue -- the codes that decide taxability per jurisdiction. "P0000000" is tangible personal property; everything else narrows from there.

top.description: How many tax codes to return.

list_tax_rules.title: List a company's tax rules
list_tax_rules.description: Read the company's custom tax rules -- overrides that change rate or taxability for particular codes and jurisdictions. These override Avalara's own content, so they are the first place to look when a rate is surprising.

create_tax_rules.title: Create tax rules
create_tax_rules.description: Add custom tax rules to a company. A rule overrides Avalara's own content for the codes and jurisdictions it matches, so a wrong one silently mis-taxes every affected sale.

tax_rules.description: The rules to create, each with `taxCode`, `taxRuleTypeId`, `jurisdictionTypeId`, `country`, `region`, `value` and effective dates.

delete_tax_rule.title: Delete a tax rule
delete_tax_rule.description: Remove a custom tax rule, so the affected transactions fall back to Avalara's own content from that point on.

output.description: Confirmation that the rule was deleted.

list_customers.title: List a company's customers
list_customers.description: Read the customer records held for exemption purposes. A customer here is matched to transactions by `customerCode`, which is how a certificate gets applied automatically.

get_customer.title: Get a customer
get_customer.description: Read one customer by their customer code, with their addresses and exemption status.

customer_code.description: Your own code for the customer.

create_customers.title: Create customers
create_customers.description: Create customer records for exemption handling. The `customerCode` must match what your transactions send, or certificates will never apply.

customers.description: The customers to create, each with `customerCode`, `name`, an address and optionally `alternateId` and contact details.

list_certificates.title: List exemption certificates
list_certificates.description: Read the company's exemption certificates, with their exposure zones, expiry dates and the customers they cover. Requires the certificate (CertCapture) subscription.

filter.description: Avalara filter expression, e.g. "valid eq true".

get_certificate.title: Get an exemption certificate
get_certificate.description: Read one certificate -- its exposure zone, exemption reason, validity dates and the customers linked to it.

list_customer_certificates.title: List a customer's certificates
list_customer_certificates.description: Read the certificates on file for one customer -- the direct answer to "why was this customer not charged tax".

customer_code.description: Your own code for the customer.

list_valid_customer_certificates.title: List a customer's valid certificates for a jurisdiction
list_valid_customer_certificates.description: Read the certificates that are actually valid for one customer in a given country and region -- what AvaTax itself consults when deciding to exempt a sale.

customer_code.description: Your own code for the customer.

output.description: The valid certificates for that jurisdiction.

link_certificates_to_customer.title: Link certificates to a customer
link_certificates_to_customer.description: Attach existing certificates to a customer, so their sales in the covered zones stop being taxed. This changes what customers are charged.

customer_code.description: Your own code for the customer.

certificate_ids.description: Ids of the certificates to link.

create_cert_express_invitation.title: Invite a customer to upload a certificate
create_cert_express_invitation.description: Send a customer a CertExpress invitation so they can upload their own exemption certificate. This emails a real customer, so check the address and the message first.

customer_code.description: Your own code for the customer.

invitation.description: The invitation -- `recipient`, `deliveryMethod` ("Email", "Fax", "Download"), `message`, and the `exposureZones` and `exemptReasons` you want covered.

output.description: The created invitation, including its link.

list_entity_use_codes.title: List entity use codes
list_entity_use_codes.description: Read Avalara's entity use codes -- the reasons a customer can be exempt (government, resale, charity, education). These are what a transaction's `entity_use_code` takes.

list_countries.title: List supported countries
list_countries.description: Read the countries AvaTax supports, with their codes and tax type coverage.

list_regions_by_country.title: List a country's regions
list_regions_by_country.description: Read the states, provinces or regions of a country with their codes -- what an address's `region` field must contain.

list_jurisdictions.title: List jurisdictions
list_jurisdictions.description: Read Avalara's jurisdiction catalogue -- every taxing authority with its code, type and rate. The reference behind any rate breakdown.

filter.description: Avalara filter expression, e.g. "region eq CA".

list_tax_authorities.title: List tax authorities
list_tax_authorities.description: Read the tax authorities Avalara knows, with their ids and jurisdiction types -- who the money is ultimately owed to.

list_parameters.title: List transaction and item parameters
list_parameters.description: Read the parameters AvaTax accepts on transactions, lines and items -- the extra facts (weight, alcohol content, delivery terms) some jurisdictions need before they can tax something correctly.

output.description: The available parameters and their value types.

list_currencies.title: List supported currencies
list_currencies.description: Read the currencies AvaTax accepts, with their codes and decimal places.

list_batches.title: List batches
list_batches.description: Read the account's batch jobs -- bulk transaction, item or certificate imports -- with their status and record counts.

filter.description: Avalara filter expression, e.g. "status eq Completed".

get_batch.title: Get a batch
get_batch.description: Read one batch job's status and per-record results -- the place to find out which rows of an import failed and why.

create_item_import_batch.title: Import items in bulk
create_item_import_batch.description: Queue a batch import of catalogue items from a file. Avalara processes it in the background -- poll get_batch until it completes.

batch.description: The batch definition, including its `name` and the file content in Avalara's batch file shape.

cancel_batch.title: Cancel a batch
cancel_batch.description: Stop a batch job that is still running. Records already processed stay processed, so a cancelled import can leave a partial result.

list_reports.title: List reports
list_reports.description: Read the account's generated reports with their status. Report generation is asynchronous, so this is how you find out whether one is ready.

page_key.description: Paging key from a previous response.

get_report.title: Get a report
get_report.description: Read one report's status and metadata; download it once it is complete.

export_audit_logs.title: Export audit logs
export_audit_logs.description: Queue an export of the account's API audit logs for a date range -- every call made, with its request and response. The forensic record when a transaction looks wrong.

request.description: The export request -- `startDate` and `endDate`, plus optional filters on company or account.

list_users.title: List users on the account
list_users.description: Read the AvaTax users on an account, with their roles and the companies each can reach.

get_user_entitlements.title: Get a user's entitlements
get_user_entitlements.description: Read what one user is actually allowed to do -- which permissions and companies their role grants. The honest answer before blaming an endpoint for a 403.

output.description: The user's permissions and company access.

list_company_settings.title: List a company's settings
list_company_settings.description: Read the company's settings -- your own key/value configuration held alongside Avalara's, used by integrations to store per-company options.

filter.description: Avalara filter expression, e.g. "set eq AvaCert".

create_company_settings.title: Create company settings
create_company_settings.description: Store settings against a company. `set`, `name` and `value` are yours to choose -- Avalara treats them as opaque configuration for your integration.
